title: FBN Storage Capacity, Overage Fees and Inbound Suspension
content:
When peak daily usage in a storage month exceeds the program's storage capacity, a capacity overage fee of the overage rate times the cubic feet above the limit is billed for that month. When the consecutive months with an overage fee reach the program's overage months for suspension, or the seller's payments balance has stayed negative longer than the unpaid fee suspension days, inbound shipments are suspended. A suspension is lifted only when its cause is cleared: for overage, a storage month billed with no overage fee; for unpaid fees, a payments balance of zero or more.

These terms govern every Fulfilled by Northloop (FBN) enrollment.

## The overage fee

The overage fee of a storage month is the peak cubic feet above the program's capacity limit multiplied by the program's overage rate per cubic foot, rounded to the cent. A month whose peak daily usage does not exceed the limit carries no overage fee.

## Counting consecutive overage months

The count runs back from the most recent billed storage month: it is the number of consecutive storage months, ending with the most recent one, that carry a capacity overage fee. A month without an overage fee ends the run.

| Recent billed storage months (hypothetical, oldest first) | Consecutive overage months |
|---|---|
| fee, fee, fee | 3 |
| fee, no fee, fee | 1 |
| fee, fee, no fee | 0 |

## Suspension and its lifting

| Cause recorded on the suspension | Suspension when | Lifted only when |
|---|---|---|
| capacity overage | the consecutive overage months reach the program's overage months for suspension | a storage month is billed with no overage fee |
| unpaid fees | the payments balance has stayed negative longer than the program's unpaid fee suspension days | the payments balance is zero or more |

A suspension moves the enrollment from active to inbound suspended and records its cause. Lifting it returns the enrollment to active and resets the recorded cause to none; lifting is a support-desk action and is possible only once the recorded cause is cleared. A suspension whose cause is not cleared stays in place.

Boundary illustration (hypothetical): in a program whose figure is 30 unpaid-fee days, a balance negative for 30 days has not stayed negative longer than 30 days; on the 31st day it has.
